# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility

---
rp1_run_id: 2ca070d6-4557-42a2-b4a2-badacf24440d
---

## Overview

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Status**: Requirements Defined
**Priority**: Must Have

This feature provides a text normalization utility that converts arbitrary text input into URL-safe, hyphenated slug format suitable for identifiers, filenames, and routing.

## Business Context

String slugification is a common requirement across web applications for:
- Generating URL-friendly identifiers from user input
- Creating consistent file naming from arbitrary text
- Normalizing text for searching and indexing

## Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Case Normalization
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must convert all alphabetic characters in the input text to lowercase.

**Rationale**: Consistent lowercase formatting ensures URL and identifier uniqueness regardless of input casing (e.g., "Hello" and "HELLO" produce the same slug).

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case normalization
- Mixed-case input like "Hello, World!" produces lowercase output

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must replace all space characters and underscore characters with single hyphens.

**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard separator in URL slugs and kebab-case identifiers. Spaces are invalid in URLs, and underscores need normalization to a single separator type.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Single space characters are replaced with single hyphens
- Multiple consecutive spaces are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
- Underscore characters are replaced with single hyphens
- Multiple consecutive underscores are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
- Mixed spaces and underscores are normalized to single hyphens

### REQ-003: Character Filtering
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), digit (0-9), or hyphen (-).

**Rationale**: URL-safe slugs should contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens. Special characters, punctuation, and symbols must be stripped to ensure compatibility across systems.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Alphabetic characters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
- Numeric digits (0-9) are retained
- Hyphens (-) are retained
- All punctuation (!, ?, ., ,, etc.) is removed
- All special characters (@, #, $, %, etc.) is removed
- Unicode characters outside basic Latin are removed

### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.

**Rationale**: Consecutive hyphens may result from multiple filtering and replacement operations. Collapsing ensures clean, readable output without repeated separators.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Two consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
- Three or more consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
- Single hyphens remain unchanged
- Hyphen collapsing occurs after all character filtering and replacement

### REQ-005: Edge Trimming
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must remove any leading or trailing hyphens from the output.

**Rationale**: Slugs should not begin or end with separators. Trimming ensures clean output suitable for use in URLs, file paths, and identifiers.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Leading hyphens are removed from the beginning of the output
- Trailing hyphens are removed from the end of the output
- Multiple leading or trailing hyphens are all removed
- Internal hyphens are preserved
- Trimming occurs as the final transformation step

### REQ-006: Function Signature
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must be exposed as a function named `slugify` that accepts a single text parameter and returns the slugified string.

**Rationale**: A clear, simple function signature ensures ease of use and integration into existing TypeScript/JavaScript codebases.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Function is named `slugify`
- Function accepts one parameter representing the input text
- Function returns a string representing the slugified output
- Function is exported for use by other modules

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Convert Display Text to URL Slug
**As a** developer
**I want** to convert user-provided display text into a URL-safe slug
**So that** I can generate clean, readable URLs from arbitrary input

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN user input "Hello, World!"
- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
- THEN I receive "hello-world"

### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers with Underscores
**As a** developer
**I want** to normalize identifiers that use underscores
**So that** I can convert snake_case or mixed formats to kebab-case

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN user input "Foo__Bar" (with multiple underscores and spaces)
- WHEN I call `slugify("  Foo__Bar  ")`
- THEN I receive "foo-bar"

### STORY-003: Clean Up Messy Input with Repeated Separators
**As a** developer
**I want** to collapse repeated hyphens from filtered characters
**So that** the output is clean and readable

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN user input "a---b" (multiple hyphens)
- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
- THEN I receive "a-b"

## Test Cases

| Input | Expected Output | Validates |
|-------|----------------|-----------|
| `"Hello, World!"` | `"hello-world"` | REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-005 |
| `"  Foo__Bar  "` | `"foo-bar"` | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-005 |
| `"a---b"` | `"a-b"` | REQ-004 |
| `"Test123"` | `"test123"` | REQ-001, REQ-003 |
| `"---trim---"` | `"trim"` | REQ-005 |
| `"multiple   spaces"` | `"multiple-spaces"` | REQ-002, REQ-004 |
| `"Special!@#$%Chars"` | `"specialchars"` | REQ-003 |
| `""` (empty string) | `""` | Edge case handling |

## Constraints

**Technical Constraints**:
- Must be implementable as a pure function (no side effects)
- Must handle empty string input gracefully
- Must be compatible with TypeScript strict mode

**Business Constraints**:
- Must process input in a single pass for performance
- Must produce deterministic output (same input always produces same output)

## Success Criteria

The feature is complete when:
1. The `slugify` function is implemented and exported
2. All test cases in the table above pass
3. The function handles edge cases (empty strings, all-special-characters)
4. Unit tests verify all requirements
5. The function integrates into the existing `src/utils.ts` module

## Out of Scope

The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
- Unicode character normalization (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents)
- Configurable separator characters (hyphen is fixed)
- Maximum length enforcement
- Custom character allow/deny lists
- Transliteration of non-Latin scripts

    10→## Overview
    11→
    12→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    13→**Status**: Requirements Defined
    14→**Priority**: Must Have
    15→
    16→This feature provides a text normalization utility that converts arbitrary text input into URL-safe, hyphenated slug format suitable for identifiers, filenames, and routing.
    17→
    18→## Business Context
    19→
    20→String slugification is a common requirement across web applications for:
    21→- Generating URL-friendly identifiers from user input
    22→- Creating consistent file naming from arbitrary text
    23→- Normalizing text for searching and indexing
    24→
    25→## Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Case Normalization
    28→**Priority**: Must Have
    29→**User Type**: Developer
    30→**Description**: The utility must convert all alphabetic characters in the input text to lowercase.
    31→
    32→**Rationale**: Consistent lowercase formatting ensures URL and identifier uniqueness regardless of input casing (e.g., "Hello" and "HELLO" produce the same slug).
    33→
    34→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    35→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    36→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    37→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case normalization
    38→- Mixed-case input like "Hello, World!" produces lowercase output
    39→
    40→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    41→**Priority**: Must Have
    42→**User Type**: Developer
    43→**Description**: The utility must replace all space characters and underscore characters with single hyphens.
    44→
    45→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard separator in URL slugs and kebab-case identifiers. Spaces are invalid in URLs, and underscores need normalization to a single separator type.
    46→
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Single space characters are replaced with single hyphens
    49→- Multiple consecutive spaces are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    50→- Underscore characters are replaced with single hyphens
    51→- Multiple consecutive underscores are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    52→- Mixed spaces and underscores are normalized to single hyphens
    53→
    54→### REQ-003: Character Filtering
    55→**Priority**: Must Have
    56→**User Type**: Developer
    57→**Description**: The utility must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), digit (0-9), or hyphen (-).
    58→
    59→**Rationale**: URL-safe slugs should contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens. Special characters, punctuation, and symbols must be stripped to ensure compatibility across systems.
    60→
    61→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    62→- Alphabetic characters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    63→- Numeric digits (0-9) are retained
    64→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    65→- All punctuation (!, ?, ., ,, etc.) is removed
    66→- All special characters (@, #, $, %, etc.) is removed
    67→- Unicode characters outside basic Latin are removed
    68→
    69→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse
    70→**Priority**: Must Have
    71→**User Type**: Developer
    72→**Description**: The utility must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    73→
    74→**Rationale**: Consecutive hyphens may result from multiple filtering and replacement operations. Collapsing ensures clean, readable output without repeated separators.
    75→
    76→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    77→- Two consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
    78→- Three or more consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
    79→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    80→- Hyphen collapsing occurs after all character filtering and replacement
    81→
    82→### REQ-005: Edge Trimming
    83→**Priority**: Must Have
    84→**User Type**: Developer
    85→**Description**: The utility must remove any leading or trailing hyphens from the output.
    86→
    87→**Rationale**: Slugs should not begin or end with separators. Trimming ensures clean output suitable for use in URLs, file paths, and identifiers.
    88→
    89→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    90→- Leading hyphens are removed from the beginning of the output
    91→- Trailing hyphens are removed from the end of the output
    92→- Multiple leading or trailing hyphens are all removed
    93→- Internal hyphens are preserved
    94→- Trimming occurs as the final transformation step
    95→
    96→### REQ-006: Function Signature
    97→**Priority**: Must Have
    98→**User Type**: Developer
    99→**Description**: The utility must be exposed as a function named `slugify` that accepts a single text parameter and returns the slugified string.
   100→

   102→

   104→- Function is named `slugify`
   105→- Function accepts one parameter representing the input text
   106→- Function returns a string representing the slugified output
   107→- Function is exported for use by other modules
   108→
   109→## User Stories
   110→
   111→### STORY-001: Convert Display Text to URL Slug
   112→**As a** developer
   113→**I want** to convert user-provided display text into a URL-safe slug
   114→**So that** I can generate clean, readable URLs from arbitrary input
   115→
   116→**Acceptance Criteria**:

   118→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   119→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   120→
   121→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers with Underscores
   122→**As a** developer
   123→**I want** to normalize identifiers that use underscores
   124→**So that** I can convert snake_case or mixed formats to kebab-case
   125→
   126→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   127→- GIVEN user input "Foo__Bar" (with multiple underscores and spaces)
   128→- WHEN I call `slugify("  Foo__Bar  ")`
   129→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   130→
   131→### STORY-003: Clean Up Messy Input with Repeated Separators
   132→**As a** developer
   133→**I want** to collapse repeated hyphens from filtered characters
   134→**So that** the output is clean and readable
   135→
   136→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   137→- GIVEN user input "a---b" (multiple hyphens)
   138→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   139→- THEN I receive "a-b"

   151→| `"Special!@#$%Chars"` | `"specialchars"` | REQ-003 |
   152→| `""` (empty string) | `""` | Edge case handling |
   153→
   154→## Constraints

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-27

## Summary

Implement a pure `slugify` function in `src/utils.ts` that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, hyphenated slug format using a sequential transformation pipeline: lowercase, replace separators, filter characters, collapse hyphens, and trim edges. The approach prioritizes simplicity and pattern consistency with existing utility functions, using built-in string methods and regex without external dependencies.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Input Text] --> B[toLowerCase]
    B --> C[Replace spaces/underscores with hyphens]
    C --> D[Remove non-alphanumeric-non-hyphen]
    D --> E[Collapse consecutive hyphens]
    E --> F[Trim leading/trailing hyphens]
    F --> G[Output Slug]
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function | utils.ts | Importing modules | `slugify(text: string): string` - Returns URL-safe slug |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Pure function implementing text-to-slug transformation pipeline with JSDoc documentation | `src/utils.ts` |
| T2 | slugify tests | Unit tests covering all requirements and edge cases per requirements test table | `src/utils.test.ts` |

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1, T2] - Function implementation and test writing can proceed in parallel; tests validate the function contract

**Dependencies**:

- None - both components can be developed independently against the contract

**Critical Path**: T1 (tests require function to exist for execution)

## Validation Plan

    44→
    45→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard separator in URL slugs and kebab-case identifiers. Spaces are invalid in URLs, and underscores need normalization to a single separator type.
    46→

    49→- Multiple consecutive spaces are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    50→- Underscore characters are replaced with single hyphens
    51→- Multiple consecutive underscores are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)

     4→# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility
     5→
     6→---
     7→rp1_run_id: 2ca070d6-4557-42a2-b4a2-badacf24440d
     8→---
     9→
    10→## Overview
    11→
    12→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    13→**Status**: Requirements Defined
    14→**Priority**: Must Have
    15→
    16→This feature provides a text normalization utility that converts arbitrary text input into URL-safe, hyphenated slug format suitable for identifiers, filenames, and routing.
    17→
    18→## Business Context
    19→
    20→String slugification is a common requirement across web applications for:
    21→- Generating URL-friendly identifiers from user input
    22→- Creating consistent file naming from arbitrary text
    23→- Normalizing text for searching and indexing
    24→
    25→## Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Case Normalization
    28→**Priority**: Must Have
    29→**User Type**: Developer
    30→**Description**: The utility must convert all alphabetic characters in the input text to lowercase.
    31→
    32→**Rationale**: Consistent lowercase formatting ensures URL and identifier uniqueness regardless of input casing (e.g., "Hello" and "HELLO" produce the same slug).
    33→
    34→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    35→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    36→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    37→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case normalization
    38→- Mixed-case input like "Hello, World!" produces lowercase output
    39→
    40→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    41→**Priority**: Must Have
    42→**User Type**: Developer
    43→**Description**: The utility must replace all space characters and underscore characters with single hyphens.
    44→
    45→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard separator in URL slugs and kebab-case identifiers. Spaces are invalid in URLs, and underscores need normalization to a single separator type.
    46→
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Single space characters are replaced with single hyphens
    49→- Multiple consecutive spaces are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    50→- Underscore characters are replaced with single hyphens
    51→- Multiple consecutive underscores are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    52→- Mixed spaces and underscores are normalized to single hyphens
    53→
    54→### REQ-003: Character Filtering
    55→**Priority**: Must Have
    56→**User Type**: Developer
    57→**Description**: The utility must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), digit (0-9), or hyphen (-).
    58→
    59→**Rationale**: URL-safe slugs should contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens. Special characters, punctuation, and symbols must be stripped to ensure compatibility across systems.
    60→
    61→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    62→- Alphabetic characters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    63→- Numeric digits (0-9) are retained
    64→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    65→- All punctuation (!, ?, ., ,, etc.) is removed
    66→- All special characters (@, #, $, %, etc.) is removed
    67→- Unicode characters outside basic Latin are removed
    68→
    69→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse
    70→**Priority**: Must Have
    71→**User Type**: Developer
    72→**Description**: The utility must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    73→
    74→**Rationale**: Consecutive hyphens may result from multiple filtering and replacement operations. Collapsing ensures clean, readable output without repeated separators.
    75→
    76→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    77→- Two consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
    78→- Three or more consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
    79→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    80→- Hyphen collapsing occurs after all character filtering and replacement
    81→
    82→### REQ-005: Edge Trimming
    83→**Priority**: Must Have
    84→**User Type**: Developer
    85→**Description**: The utility must remove any leading or trailing hyphens from the output.
    86→
    87→**Rationale**: Slugs should not begin or end with separators. Trimming ensures clean output suitable for use in URLs, file paths, and identifiers.
    88→
    89→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    90→- Leading hyphens are removed from the beginning of the output
    91→- Trailing hyphens are removed from the end of the output
    92→- Multiple leading or trailing hyphens are all removed
    93→- Internal hyphens are preserved
    94→- Trimming occurs as the final transformation step
    95→
    96→### REQ-006: Function Signature
    97→**Priority**: Must Have
    98→**User Type**: Developer
    99→**Description**: The utility must be exposed as a function named `slugify` that accepts a single text parameter and returns the slugified string.
   100→
   101→**Rationale**: A clear, simple function signature ensures ease of use and integration into existing TypeScript/JavaScript codebases.
   102→
   103→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   104→- Function is named `slugify`
   105→- Function accepts one parameter representing the input text
   106→- Function returns a string representing the slugified output
   107→- Function is exported for use by other modules
   108→
   109→## User Stories
   110→
   111→### STORY-001: Convert Display Text to URL Slug
   112→**As a** developer
   113→**I want** to convert user-provided display text into a URL-safe slug
   114→**So that** I can generate clean, readable URLs from arbitrary input
   115→
   116→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   117→- GIVEN user input "Hello, World!"
   118→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   119→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   120→
   121→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers with Underscores
   122→**As a** developer
   123→**I want** to normalize identifiers that use underscores
   124→**So that** I can convert snake_case or mixed formats to kebab-case
   125→
   126→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   127→- GIVEN user input "Foo__Bar" (with multiple underscores and spaces)
   128→- WHEN I call `slugify("  Foo__Bar  ")`
   129→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   130→
   131→### STORY-003: Clean Up Messy Input with Repeated Separators
   132→**As a** developer
   133→**I want** to collapse repeated hyphens from filtered characters
   134→**So that** the output is clean and readable
   135→
   136→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   137→- GIVEN user input "a---b" (multiple hyphens)
   138→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   139→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   140→
   141→## Test Cases
   142→
   143→| Input | Expected Output | Validates |
   144→|-------|----------------|-----------|
   145→| `"Hello, World!"` | `"hello-world"` | REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-005 |
   146→| `"  Foo__Bar  "` | `"foo-bar"` | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-005 |
   147→| `"a---b"` | `"a-b"` | REQ-004 |
   148→| `"Test123"` | `"test123"` | REQ-001, REQ-003 |
   149→| `"---trim---"` | `"trim"` | REQ-005 |
   150→| `"multiple   spaces"` | `"multiple-spaces"` | REQ-002, REQ-004 |
   151→| `"Special!@#$%Chars"` | `"specialchars"` | REQ-003 |
   152→| `""` (empty string) | `""` | Edge case handling |
   153→
   154→## Constraints
   155→
   156→**Technical Constraints**:
   157→- Must be implementable as a pure function (no side effects)
   158→- Must handle empty string input gracefully
   159→- Must be compatible with TypeScript strict mode
   160→
   161→**Business Constraints**:
   162→- Must process input in a single pass for performance
   163→- Must produce deterministic output (same input always produces same output)
   164→
   165→## Success Criteria
   166→
   167→The feature is complete when:
   168→1. The `slugify` function is implemented and exported
   169→2. All test cases in the table above pass
   170→3. The function handles edge cases (empty strings, all-special-characters)
   171→4. Unit tests verify all requirements
   172→5. The function integrates into the existing `src/utils.ts` module
   173→
   174→## Out of Scope
   175→
   176→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   177→- Unicode character normalization (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents)
   178→- Configurable separator characters (hyphen is fixed)
   179→- Maximum length enforcement
   180→- Custom character allow/deny lists
   181→- Transliteration of non-Latin scripts
   182→
   183→---
   184→
   185→## AFK Mode Execution Log
   186→
   187→**PRD Selection**: No PRD directory found. Proceeding without parent PRD association.
   188→
   189→**Inferred Decisions**:
   190→1. **Target Module**: Inferred `src/utils.ts` as implementation location based on KB modules.md indicating utils.ts contains "reusable utility functions"
   191→2. **Export Style**: Inferred named export based on patterns.md indicating ESM modules
   192→3. **Character Set**: Inferred basic Latin alphanumeric (a-z, 0-9) based on common slug requirements
   193→4. **Edge Cases**: Inferred empty string should return empty string (graceful degradation)
   194→5. **Performance**: Inferred single-pass processing requirement as best practice for utility functions
   195→
   196→**Ambiguity Resolutions**:
   197→- "Lowercase the text": Applied to all alphabetic characters (REQ-001)
   198→- "Replace spaces and underscores": Interpreted as normalizing both to hyphens with collapse (REQ-002)
   199→- "Drop any character": Interpreted as removing characters not in allowed set (REQ-003)
   200→- "Collapse repeated hyphens": Applied after all other transformations (REQ-004)
   201→- "Trim hyphens": Applied as final step to both leading and trailing (REQ-005)
   202→
   203→---

/**
 * Add two numbers.
 */
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}

/**
 * Convert arbitrary text into a URL-safe, hyphenated slug.
 *
 * Applies the following transformations in sequence:
 * 1. Convert to lowercase
 * 2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
 * 3. Remove characters that are not letters, digits, or hyphens
 * 4. Collapse consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
 * 5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
 *
 * @param text - The input text to slugify
 * @returns A URL-safe slug string
 */
export function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')
    .replace(/-+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-|-$/g, '');
}

     3→---
     4→# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility
     5→
     6→---
     7→rp1_run_id: 2ca070d6-4557-42a2-b4a2-badacf24440d
     8→---
     9→
    10→## Overview
    11→
    12→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    13→**Status**: Requirements Defined
    14→**Priority**: Must Have
    15→
    16→This feature provides a text normalization utility that converts arbitrary text input into URL-safe, hyphenated slug format suitable for identifiers, filenames, and routing.
    17→
    18→## Business Context
    19→
    20→String slugification is a common requirement across web applications for:
    21→- Generating URL-friendly identifiers from user input
    22→- Creating consistent file naming from arbitrary text
    23→- Normalizing text for searching and indexing
    24→
    25→## Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Case Normalization
    28→**Priority**: Must Have
    29→**User Type**: Developer
    30→**Description**: The utility must convert all alphabetic characters in the input text to lowercase.
    31→
    32→**Rationale**: Consistent lowercase formatting ensures URL and identifier uniqueness regardless of input casing (e.g., "Hello" and "HELLO" produce the same slug).
    33→
    34→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    35→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    36→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    37→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case normalization
    38→- Mixed-case input like "Hello, World!" produces lowercase output
    39→
    40→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    41→**Priority**: Must Have
    42→**User Type**: Developer
    43→**Description**: The utility must replace all space characters and underscore characters with single hyphens.
    44→
    45→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard separator in URL slugs and kebab-case identifiers. Spaces are invalid in URLs, and underscores need normalization to a single separator type.
    46→
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Single space characters are replaced with single hyphens
    49→- Multiple consecutive spaces are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    50→- Underscore characters are replaced with single hyphens
    51→- Multiple consecutive underscores are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    52→- Mixed spaces and underscores are normalized to single hyphens
    53→
    54→### REQ-003: Character Filtering
    55→**Priority**: Must Have
    56→**User Type**: Developer
    57→**Description**: The utility must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), digit (0-9), or hyphen (-).
    58→
    59→**Rationale**: URL-safe slugs should contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens. Special characters, punctuation, and symbols must be stripped to ensure compatibility across systems.
    60→
    61→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    62→- Alphabetic characters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    63→- Numeric digits (0-9) are retained
    64→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    65→- All punctuation (!, ?, ., ,, etc.) is removed
    66→- All special characters (@, #, $, %, etc.) is removed
    67→- Unicode characters outside basic Latin are removed
    68→
    69→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse
    70→**Priority**: Must Have
    71→**User Type**: Developer
    72→**Description**: The utility must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    73→
    74→**Rationale**: Consecutive hyphens may result from multiple filtering and replacement operations. Collapsing ensures clean, readable output without repeated separators.
    75→
    76→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    77→- Two consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
    78→- Three or more consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
    79→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    80→- Hyphen collapsing occurs after all character filtering and replacement
    81→
    82→### REQ-005: Edge Trimming
    83→**Priority**: Must Have
    84→**User Type**: Developer
    85→**Description**: The utility must remove any leading or trailing hyphens from the output.
    86→
    87→**Rationale**: Slugs should not begin or end with separators. Trimming ensures clean output suitable for use in URLs, file paths, and identifiers.
    88→
    89→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    90→- Leading hyphens are removed from the beginning of the output
    91→- Trailing hyphens are removed from the end of the output
    92→- Multiple leading or trailing hyphens are all removed
    93→- Internal hyphens are preserved
    94→- Trimming occurs as the final transformation step
    95→
    96→### REQ-006: Function Signature
    97→**Priority**: Must Have
    98→**User Type**: Developer
    99→**Description**: The utility must be exposed as a function named `slugify` that accepts a single text parameter and returns the slugified string.
   100→
   101→**Rationale**: A clear, simple function signature ensures ease of use and integration into existing TypeScript/JavaScript codebases.
   102→
   103→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   104→- Function is named `slugify`
   105→- Function accepts one parameter representing the input text
   106→- Function returns a string representing the slugified output
   107→- Function is exported for use by other modules
   108→
   109→## User Stories
   110→
   111→### STORY-001: Convert Display Text to URL Slug
   112→**As a** developer
   113→**I want** to convert user-provided display text into a URL-safe slug
   114→**So that** I can generate clean, readable URLs from arbitrary input
   115→
   116→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   117→- GIVEN user input "Hello, World!"
   118→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   119→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   120→
   121→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers with Underscores
   122→**As a** developer
   123→**I want** to normalize identifiers that use underscores
   124→**So that** I can convert snake_case or mixed formats to kebab-case
   125→
   126→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   127→- GIVEN user input "Foo__Bar" (with multiple underscores and spaces)
   128→- WHEN I call `slugify("  Foo__Bar  ")`
   129→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   130→
   131→### STORY-003: Clean Up Messy Input with Repeated Separators
   132→**As a** developer
   133→**I want** to collapse repeated hyphens from filtered characters
   134→**So that** the output is clean and readable
   135→
   136→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   137→- GIVEN user input "a---b" (multiple hyphens)
   138→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   139→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   140→
   141→## Test Cases
   142→
   143→| Input | Expected Output | Validates |
   144→|-------|----------------|-----------|
   145→| `"Hello, World!"` | `"hello-world"` | REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-005 |
   146→| `"  Foo__Bar  "` | `"foo-bar"` | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-005 |
   147→| `"a---b"` | `"a-b"` | REQ-004 |
   148→| `"Test123"` | `"test123"` | REQ-001, REQ-003 |
   149→| `"---trim---"` | `"trim"` | REQ-005 |
   150→| `"multiple   spaces"` | `"multiple-spaces"` | REQ-002, REQ-004 |
   151→| `"Special!@#$%Chars"` | `"specialchars"` | REQ-003 |
   152→| `""` (empty string) | `""` | Edge case handling |
   153→
   154→## Constraints
   155→
   156→**Technical Constraints**:
   157→- Must be implementable as a pure function (no side effects)
   158→- Must handle empty string input gracefully
   159→- Must be compatible with TypeScript strict mode
   160→
   161→**Business Constraints**:
   162→- Must process input in a single pass for performance
   163→- Must produce deterministic output (same input always produces same output)
   164→
   165→## Success Criteria
   166→
   167→The feature is complete when:
   168→1. The `slugify` function is implemented and exported
   169→2. All test cases in the table above pass
   170→3. The function handles edge cases (empty strings, all-special-characters)
   171→4. Unit tests verify all requirements
   172→5. The function integrates into the existing `src/utils.ts` module
   173→
   174→## Out of Scope
   175→
   176→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   177→- Unicode character normalization (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents)
   178→- Configurable separator characters (hyphen is fixed)
   179→- Maximum length enforcement
   180→- Custom character allow/deny lists
   181→- Transliteration of non-Latin scripts
   182→

   184→
   185→## AFK Mode Execution Log
   186→

   188→
   189→**Inferred Decisions**:
   190→1. **Target Module**: Inferred `src/utils.ts` as implementation location based on KB modules.md indicating utils.ts contains "reusable utility functions"
   191→2. **Export Style**: Inferred named export based on patterns.md indicating ESM modules
   192→3. **Character Set**: Inferred basic Latin alphanumeric (a-z, 0-9) based on common slug requirements
   193→4. **Edge Cases**: Inferred empty string should return empty string (graceful degradation)
   194→5. **Performance**: Inferred single-pass processing requirement as best practice for utility functions
   195→
   196→**Ambiguity Resolutions**:
   197→- "Lowercase the text": Applied to all alphabetic characters (REQ-001)
   198→- "Replace spaces and underscores": Interpreted as normalizing both to hyphens with collapse (REQ-002)
   199→- "Drop any character": Interpreted as removing characters not in allowed set (REQ-003)
   200→- "Collapse repeated hyphens": Applied after all other transformations (REQ-004)
   201→- "Trim hyphens": Applied as final step to both leading and trailing (REQ-005)
   202→

# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility

---
rp1_run_id: 2ca070d6-4557-42a2-b4a2-badacf24440d
---

## Overview

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Status**: Requirements Defined
**Priority**: Must Have

This feature provides a text normalization utility that converts arbitrary text input into URL-safe, hyphenated slug format suitable for identifiers, filenames, and routing.

## Business Context

String slugification is a common requirement across web applications for:
- Generating URL-friendly identifiers from user input
- Creating consistent file naming from arbitrary text
- Normalizing text for searching and indexing

## Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Case Normalization
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must convert all alphabetic characters in the input text to lowercase.

**Rationale**: Consistent lowercase formatting ensures URL and identifier uniqueness regardless of input casing (e.g., "Hello" and "HELLO" produce the same slug).

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case normalization
- Mixed-case input like "Hello, World!" produces lowercase output

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must replace all space characters and underscore characters with single hyphens.

**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard separator in URL slugs and kebab-case identifiers. Spaces are invalid in URLs, and underscores need normalization to a single separator type.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Single space characters are replaced with single hyphens
- Multiple consecutive spaces are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
- Underscore characters are replaced with single hyphens
- Multiple consecutive underscores are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
- Mixed spaces and underscores are normalized to single hyphens

### REQ-003: Character Filtering
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), digit (0-9), or hyphen (-).

**Rationale**: URL-safe slugs should contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens. Special characters, punctuation, and symbols must be stripped to ensure compatibility across systems.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Alphabetic characters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
- Numeric digits (0-9) are retained
- Hyphens (-) are retained
- All punctuation (!, ?, ., ,, etc.) is removed
- All special characters (@, #, $, %, etc.) is removed
- Unicode characters outside basic Latin are removed

### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.

**Rationale**: Consecutive hyphens may result from multiple filtering and replacement operations. Collapsing ensures clean, readable output without repeated separators.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Two consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
- Three or more consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
- Single hyphens remain unchanged
- Hyphen collapsing occurs after all character filtering and replacement

### REQ-005: Edge Trimming
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must remove any leading or trailing hyphens from the output.

**Rationale**: Slugs should not begin or end with separators. Trimming ensures clean output suitable for use in URLs, file paths, and identifiers.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Leading hyphens are removed from the beginning of the output
- Trailing hyphens are removed from the end of the output
- Multiple leading or trailing hyphens are all removed
- Internal hyphens are preserved
- Trimming occurs as the final transformation step

### REQ-006: Function Signature
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The utility must be exposed as a function named `slugify` that accepts a single text parameter and returns the slugified string.

**Rationale**: A clear, simple function signature ensures ease of use and integration into existing TypeScript/JavaScript codebases.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Function is named `slugify`
- Function accepts one parameter representing the input text
- Function returns a string representing the slugified output
- Function is exported for use by other modules

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Convert Display Text to URL Slug
**As a** developer
**I want** to convert user-provided display text into a URL-safe slug
**So that** I can generate clean, readable URLs from arbitrary input

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN user input "Hello, World!"
- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
- THEN I receive "hello-world"

### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers with Underscores
**As a** developer
**I want** to normalize identifiers that use underscores
**So that** I can convert snake_case or mixed formats to kebab-case

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN user input "Foo__Bar" (with multiple underscores and spaces)
- WHEN I call `slugify("  Foo__Bar  ")`
- THEN I receive "foo-bar"

### STORY-003: Clean Up Messy Input with Repeated Separators
**As a** developer
**I want** to collapse repeated hyphens from filtered characters
**So that** the output is clean and readable

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN user input "a---b" (multiple hyphens)
- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
- THEN I receive "a-b"

## Test Cases

| Input | Expected Output | Validates |
|-------|----------------|-----------|
| `"Hello, World!"` | `"hello-world"` | REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-005 |
| `"  Foo__Bar  "` | `"foo-bar"` | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-005 |
| `"a---b"` | `"a-b"` | REQ-004 |
| `"Test123"` | `"test123"` | REQ-001, REQ-003 |
| `"---trim---"` | `"trim"` | REQ-005 |
| `"multiple   spaces"` | `"multiple-spaces"` | REQ-002, REQ-004 |
| `"Special!@#$%Chars"` | `"specialchars"` | REQ-003 |
| `""` (empty string) | `""` | Edge case handling |

## Constraints

**Technical Constraints**:
- Must be implementable as a pure function (no side effects)
- Must handle empty string input gracefully
- Must be compatible with TypeScript strict mode

**Business Constraints**:
- Must process input in a single pass for performance
- Must produce deterministic output (same input always produces same output)

## Success Criteria

The feature is complete when:
1. The `slugify` function is implemented and exported
2. All test cases in the table above pass
3. The function handles edge cases (empty strings, all-special-characters)
4. Unit tests verify all requirements
5. The function integrates into the existing `src/utils.ts` module

## Out of Scope

The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
- Unicode character normalization (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents)
- Configurable separator characters (hyphen is fixed)
- Maximum length enforcement
- Custom character allow/deny lists
- Transliteration of non-Latin scripts

---

## AFK Mode Execution Log

**PRD Selection**: No PRD directory found. Proceeding without parent PRD association.

**Inferred Decisions**:
1. **Target Module**: Inferred `src/utils.ts` as implementation location based on KB modules.md indicating utils.ts contains "reusable utility functions"
2. **Export Style**: Inferred named export based on patterns.md indicating ESM modules
3. **Character Set**: Inferred basic Latin alphanumeric (a-z, 0-9) based on common slug requirements
4. **Edge Cases**: Inferred empty string should return empty string (graceful degradation)
5. **Performance**: Inferred single-pass processing requirement as best practice for utility functions

**Ambiguity Resolutions**:
- "Lowercase the text": Applied to all alphabetic characters (REQ-001)
- "Replace spaces and underscores": Interpreted as normalizing both to hyphens with collapse (REQ-002)
- "Drop any character": Interpreted as removing characters not in allowed set (REQ-003)
- "Collapse repeated hyphens": Applied after all other transformations (REQ-004)
- "Trim hyphens": Applied as final step to both leading and trailing (REQ-005)

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-27

## Summary

Implement a pure `slugify` function in `src/utils.ts` that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe, hyphenated slug format using a sequential transformation pipeline: lowercase, replace separators, filter characters, collapse hyphens, and trim edges. The approach prioritizes simplicity and pattern consistency with existing utility functions, using built-in string methods and regex without external dependencies.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Input Text] --> B[toLowerCase]
    B --> C[Replace spaces/underscores with hyphens]
    C --> D[Remove non-alphanumeric-non-hyphen]
    D --> E[Collapse consecutive hyphens]
    E --> F[Trim leading/trailing hyphens]
    F --> G[Output Slug]
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function | utils.ts | Importing modules | `slugify(text: string): string` - Returns URL-safe slug |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Pure function implementing text-to-slug transformation pipeline with JSDoc documentation | `src/utils.ts` |
| T2 | slugify tests | Unit tests covering all requirements and edge cases per requirements test table | `src/utils.test.ts` |

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1, T2] - Function implementation and test writing can proceed in parallel; tests validate the function contract

**Dependencies**:

- None - both components can be developed independently against the contract

**Critical Path**: T1 (tests require function to exist for execution)

## Validation Plan

| Behavior Or Contract | Failure Mode Covered | Test Type | Evidence Or Command |
|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| Case normalization (REQ-001) | Mixed case not lowercased | unit | `bun test` - "Hello, World!" -> "hello-world" |
| Space/underscore replacement (REQ-002) | Spaces or underscores retained | unit | `bun test` - "  Foo__Bar  " -> "foo-bar" |
| Character filtering (REQ-003) | Special characters retained | unit | `bun test` - "Special!@#$%Chars" -> "specialchars" |
| Hyphen collapse (REQ-004) | Multiple hyphens not collapsed | unit | `bun test` - "a---b" -> "a-b" |
| Edge trimming (REQ-005) | Leading/trailing hyphens retained | unit | `bun test` - "---trim---" -> "trim" |
| Function signature (REQ-006) | Wrong name or signature | unit | Import test verifies named export |
| Empty string handling | Crash on empty input | unit | `bun test` - "" -> "" |

## Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| edit | .rp1/context/modules.md | Utils section | modules.md:Utils | Add slugify to documented utility functions |

## Open Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Unicode input produces unexpected output | LOW | Requirements explicitly exclude Unicode normalization; filtered characters are removed per spec |

# Design Decisions: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Created**: 2026-07-27

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Implementation location | `src/utils.ts` | Follows existing pattern of utility functions in utils module; KB modules.md specifies utils.ts for "reusable utility functions" | Separate `src/slugify.ts` module (rejected: inconsistent with existing simple utility structure) |
| D2 | Export style | Named export | Consistent with existing `greet` and `add` exports; KB patterns.md specifies ESM modules | Default export (rejected: breaks consistency with existing codebase pattern) |
| D3 | Implementation approach | Sequential method chaining with regex | Pure function using built-in string methods; no external dependencies needed for this transformation | External library like `slugify` npm package (rejected: adds dependency contrary to project pattern of no external deps) |
| D4 | Transformation order | lowercase -> replace separators -> filter -> collapse -> trim | Order ensures correct behavior: filtering after replacement prevents orphaned hyphens; collapsing before trimming handles edge cases | Alternative orderings (rejected: could leave artifacts from intermediate steps) |
| D5 | Empty string handling | Return empty string | Graceful degradation; empty input produces empty output without errors | Throw error (rejected: unnecessary for utility function; caller can validate if needed) |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Source | Rationale |
|----------|--------|--------|-----------|
| Target module | `src/utils.ts` | KB modules.md | Utils module documented as location for "reusable utility functions" |
| Test framework | Bun test runner | KB patterns.md | Project uses Bun's built-in test runner with describe/test/expect pattern |
| Test file location | `src/utils.test.ts` | KB patterns.md | Tests co-located with source as `*.test.ts` |
| Function naming | camelCase (`slugify`) | KB patterns.md | Functions use camelCase per project naming conventions |
| Documentation style | JSDoc comments | Codebase pattern | Existing functions in utils.ts use JSDoc block comments |
| Type annotations | TypeScript strict mode | KB patterns.md | Project uses TypeScript strict mode |

    10→## Overview
    11→
    12→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    13→**Status**: Requirements Defined
    14→**Priority**: Must Have
    15→
    16→This feature provides a text normalization utility that converts arbitrary text input into URL-safe, hyphenated slug format suitable for identifiers, filenames, and routing.
    17→
    18→## Business Context
    19→
    20→String slugification is a common requirement across web applications for:
    21→- Generating URL-friendly identifiers from user input
    22→- Creating consistent file naming from arbitrary text
    23→- Normalizing text for searching and indexing
    24→
    25→## Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Case Normalization
    28→**Priority**: Must Have
    29→**User Type**: Developer
    30→**Description**: The utility must convert all alphabetic characters in the input text to lowercase.
    31→
    32→**Rationale**: Consistent lowercase formatting ensures URL and identifier uniqueness regardless of input casing (e.g., "Hello" and "HELLO" produce the same slug).
    33→
    34→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    35→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    36→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    37→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case normalization
    38→- Mixed-case input like "Hello, World!" produces lowercase output
    39→
    40→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    41→**Priority**: Must Have
    42→**User Type**: Developer
    43→**Description**: The utility must replace all space characters and underscore characters with single hyphens.
    44→
    45→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard separator in URL slugs and kebab-case identifiers. Spaces are invalid in URLs, and underscores need normalization to a single separator type.
    46→
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Single space characters are replaced with single hyphens
    49→- Multiple consecutive spaces are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    50→- Underscore characters are replaced with single hyphens
    51→- Multiple consecutive underscores are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    52→- Mixed spaces and underscores are normalized to single hyphens
    53→
    54→### REQ-003: Character Filtering
    55→**Priority**: Must Have
    56→**User Type**: Developer
    57→**Description**: The utility must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), digit (0-9), or hyphen (-).
    58→
    59→**Rationale**: URL-safe slugs should contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens. Special characters, punctuation, and symbols must be stripped to ensure compatibility across systems.
    60→
    61→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    62→- Alphabetic characters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    63→- Numeric digits (0-9) are retained
    64→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    65→- All punctuation (!, ?, ., ,, etc.) is removed
    66→- All special characters (@, #, $, %, etc.) is removed
    67→- Unicode characters outside basic Latin are removed
    68→
    69→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse
    70→**Priority**: Must Have
    71→**User Type**: Developer
    72→**Description**: The utility must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    73→
    74→**Rationale**: Consecutive hyphens may result from multiple filtering and replacement operations. Collapsing ensures clean, readable output without repeated separators.
    75→
    76→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    77→- Two consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
    78→- Three or more consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
    79→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    80→- Hyphen collapsing occurs after all character filtering and replacement
    81→
    82→### REQ-005: Edge Trimming
    83→**Priority**: Must Have
    84→**User Type**: Developer
    85→**Description**: The utility must remove any leading or trailing hyphens from the output.
    86→
    87→**Rationale**: Slugs should not begin or end with separators. Trimming ensures clean output suitable for use in URLs, file paths, and identifiers.
    88→
    89→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    90→- Leading hyphens are removed from the beginning of the output
    91→- Trailing hyphens are removed from the end of the output
    92→- Multiple leading or trailing hyphens are all removed
    93→- Internal hyphens are preserved
    94→- Trimming occurs as the final transformation step
    95→
    96→### REQ-006: Function Signature
    97→**Priority**: Must Have
    98→**User Type**: Developer
    99→**Description**: The utility must be exposed as a function named `slugify` that accepts a single text parameter and returns the slugified string.
   100→
   101→**Rationale**: A clear, simple function signature ensures ease of use and integration into existing TypeScript/JavaScript codebases.
   102→
   103→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   104→- Function is named `slugify`
   105→- Function accepts one parameter representing the input text
   106→- Function returns a string representing the slugified output
   107→- Function is exported for use by other modules
   108→
   109→## User Stories
   110→
   111→### STORY-001: Convert Display Text to URL Slug
   112→**As a** developer
   113→**I want** to convert user-provided display text into a URL-safe slug
   114→**So that** I can generate clean, readable URLs from arbitrary input
   115→
   116→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   117→- GIVEN user input "Hello, World!"
   118→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   119→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   120→
   121→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers with Underscores
   122→**As a** developer
   123→**I want** to normalize identifiers that use underscores
   124→**So that** I can convert snake_case or mixed formats to kebab-case
   125→
   126→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   127→- GIVEN user input "Foo__Bar" (with multiple underscores and spaces)
   128→- WHEN I call `slugify("  Foo__Bar  ")`
   129→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   130→
   131→### STORY-003: Clean Up Messy Input with Repeated Separators
   132→**As a** developer
   133→**I want** to collapse repeated hyphens from filtered characters
   134→**So that** the output is clean and readable
   135→
   136→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   137→- GIVEN user input "a---b" (multiple hyphens)
   138→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   139→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   140→
   141→## Test Cases
   142→
   143→| Input | Expected Output | Validates |
   144→|-------|----------------|-----------|
   145→| `"Hello, World!"` | `"hello-world"` | REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-005 |
   146→| `"  Foo__Bar  "` | `"foo-bar"` | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-005 |
   147→| `"a---b"` | `"a-b"` | REQ-004 |
   148→| `"Test123"` | `"test123"` | REQ-001, REQ-003 |
   149→| `"---trim---"` | `"trim"` | REQ-005 |
   150→| `"multiple   spaces"` | `"multiple-spaces"` | REQ-002, REQ-004 |
   151→| `"Special!@#$%Chars"` | `"specialchars"` | REQ-003 |
   152→| `""` (empty string) | `""` | Edge case handling |
   153→
   154→## Constraints
   155→
   156→**Technical Constraints**:
   157→- Must be implementable as a pure function (no side effects)
   158→- Must handle empty string input gracefully
   159→- Must be compatible with TypeScript strict mode
   160→
   161→**Business Constraints**:
   162→- Must process input in a single pass for performance
   163→- Must produce deterministic output (same input always produces same output)
   164→
   165→## Success Criteria
   166→
   167→The feature is complete when:
   168→1. The `slugify` function is implemented and exported
   169→2. All test cases in the table above pass
   170→3. The function handles edge cases (empty strings, all-special-characters)
   171→4. Unit tests verify all requirements
   172→5. The function integrates into the existing `src/utils.ts` module
   173→
   174→## Out of Scope
   175→
   176→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   177→- Unicode character normalization (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents)
   178→- Configurable separator characters (hyphen is fixed)
   179→- Maximum length enforcement

# Feature Tasks: slugify-utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Status**: Planning
**Created**: 2026-07-27

## Overview

This document defines the implementation tasks for the slugify-utility feature, which provides a pure function for converting arbitrary text into URL-safe, hyphenated slug format. The implementation follows a sequential transformation pipeline: lowercase, replace separators, filter characters, collapse hyphens, and trim edges.

## Task Index

| ID | Type | Status | Complexity | Acceptance Refs | Dependencies | Target |
|----|------|--------|------------|-----------------|--------------|--------|
| T1 | code | pending | simple | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006 | [] | src/utils.ts |
| T2 | code | pending | simple | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006 | [] | src/utils.test.ts |
| TD1 | docs | pending | simple | - | [] | .rp1/context/modules.md |

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1, T2] - Function implementation and test writing can proceed in parallel; tests validate the function contract

**Dependencies**:

- None - both components can be developed independently against the contract

**Critical Path**: T1 (tests require function to exist for execution)

## Task Breakdown

### Core Implementation

- [ ] **T1**: Implement slugify function with transformation pipeline `[complexity:simple]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#component-plan](design.md#component-plan)

    **Acceptance Refs**: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006

    **Depends On**: -

    **Effort**: 2 hours

    **Acceptance Criteria**:

    - [ ] Function named `slugify` exported from `src/utils.ts`
    - [ ] Accepts single string parameter, returns string
    - [ ] Implements sequential pipeline: toLowerCase -> replace spaces/underscores with hyphens -> filter to alphanumeric+hyphen -> collapse consecutive hyphens -> trim leading/trailing hyphens
    - [ ] Pure function with no side effects
    - [ ] Includes JSDoc documentation describing function purpose and parameters
    - [ ] TypeScript strict mode compatible

- [ ] **T2**: Add comprehensive unit tests for slugify function `[complexity:simple]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#validation-plan](design.md#validation-plan)

    **Acceptance Refs**: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006

    **Depends On**: -

    **Effort**: 1.5 hours

    **Acceptance Criteria**:

    - [ ] Test case: "Hello, World!" -> "hello-world" (REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-005)
    - [ ] Test case: "  Foo__Bar  " -> "foo-bar" (REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-005)
    - [ ] Test case: "a---b" -> "a-b" (REQ-004)
    - [ ] Test case: "Test123" -> "test123" (REQ-001, REQ-003)
    - [ ] Test case: "---trim---" -> "trim" (REQ-005)
    - [ ] Test case: "multiple   spaces" -> "multiple-spaces" (REQ-002, REQ-004)
    - [ ] Test case: "Special!@#$%Chars" -> "specialchars" (REQ-003)
    - [ ] Test case: empty string "" -> "" (edge case)
    - [ ] Verify function import and signature (REQ-006)
    - [ ] All tests pass with `bun test`

### Documentation

- [ ] **TD1**: Update modules.md - Utils section `[complexity:simple]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#documentation-impact](design.md#documentation-impact)

    **Type**: edit

    **Target**: .rp1/context/modules.md

    **Section**: Utils section

    **KB Source**: modules.md:Utils

    **Effort**: 30 minutes

    **Acceptance Criteria**:

    - [ ] Section reflects addition of slugify function to utils module
    - [ ] Description includes function signature and purpose
    - [ ] No broken links in updated section

## Task Subflow

```mermaid
graph TD
    Start([Start]) --> T1[T1: Implement slugify function]
    Start --> T2[T2: Add unit tests]
    T1 --> TD1[TD1: Update modules.md]
    T2 --> TD1
    TD1 --> End([Complete])

    style T1 fill:#e1f5ff
    style T2 fill:#e1f5ff
    style TD1 fill:#fff4e1
```

## Effort Summary

- **Total Tasks**: 3 (2 code + 1 docs)
- **Total Effort**: 4 hours
- **Estimated Duration**: 0.5 days

     4→# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility
     5→
     6→---

     8→---
     9→
    10→## Overview
    11→
    12→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    13→**Status**: Requirements Defined
    14→**Priority**: Must Have
    15→
    16→This feature provides a text normalization utility that converts arbitrary text input into URL-safe, hyphenated slug format suitable for identifiers, filenames, and routing.
    17→
    18→## Business Context
    19→
    20→String slugification is a common requirement across web applications for:
    21→- Generating URL-friendly identifiers from user input
    22→- Creating consistent file naming from arbitrary text
    23→- Normalizing text for searching and indexing
    24→
    25→## Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Case Normalization
    28→**Priority**: Must Have
    29→**User Type**: Developer
    30→**Description**: The utility must convert all alphabetic characters in the input text to lowercase.
    31→
    32→**Rationale**: Consistent lowercase formatting ensures URL and identifier uniqueness regardless of input casing (e.g., "Hello" and "HELLO" produce the same slug).
    33→
    34→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    35→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    36→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    37→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case normalization
    38→- Mixed-case input like "Hello, World!" produces lowercase output
    39→
    40→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    41→**Priority**: Must Have
    42→**User Type**: Developer
    43→**Description**: The utility must replace all space characters and underscore characters with single hyphens.
    44→
    45→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard separator in URL slugs and kebab-case identifiers. Spaces are invalid in URLs, and underscores need normalization to a single separator type.
    46→
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Single space characters are replaced with single hyphens
    49→- Multiple consecutive spaces are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    50→- Underscore characters are replaced with single hyphens
    51→- Multiple consecutive underscores are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    52→- Mixed spaces and underscores are normalized to single hyphens
    53→
    54→### REQ-003: Character Filtering
    55→**Priority**: Must Have
    56→**User Type**: Developer
    57→**Description**: The utility must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), digit (0-9), or hyphen (-).
    58→
    59→**Rationale**: URL-safe slugs should contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens. Special characters, punctuation, and symbols must be stripped to ensure compatibility across systems.
    60→
    61→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    62→- Alphabetic characters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    63→- Numeric digits (0-9) are retained
    64→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    65→- All punctuation (!, ?, ., ,, etc.) is removed
    66→- All special characters (@, #, $, %, etc.) is removed
    67→- Unicode characters outside basic Latin are removed
    68→
    69→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse
    70→**Priority**: Must Have
    71→**User Type**: Developer
    72→**Description**: The utility must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    73→
    74→**Rationale**: Consecutive hyphens may result from multiple filtering and replacement operations. Collapsing ensures clean, readable output without repeated separators.
    75→
    76→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    77→- Two consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
    78→- Three or more consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
    79→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    80→- Hyphen collapsing occurs after all character filtering and replacement
    81→
    82→### REQ-005: Edge Trimming
    83→**Priority**: Must Have
    84→**User Type**: Developer
    85→**Description**: The utility must remove any leading or trailing hyphens from the output.
    86→
    87→**Rationale**: Slugs should not begin or end with separators. Trimming ensures clean output suitable for use in URLs, file paths, and identifiers.
    88→
    89→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    90→- Leading hyphens are removed from the beginning of the output
    91→- Trailing hyphens are removed from the end of the output
    92→- Multiple leading or trailing hyphens are all removed
    93→- Internal hyphens are preserved
    94→- Trimming occurs as the final transformation step
    95→
    96→### REQ-006: Function Signature
    97→**Priority**: Must Have
    98→**User Type**: Developer
    99→**Description**: The utility must be exposed as a function named `slugify` that accepts a single text parameter and returns the slugified string.
   100→
   101→**Rationale**: A clear, simple function signature ensures ease of use and integration into existing TypeScript/JavaScript codebases.
   102→
   103→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   104→- Function is named `slugify`
   105→- Function accepts one parameter representing the input text
   106→- Function returns a string representing the slugified output
   107→- Function is exported for use by other modules
   108→
   109→## User Stories
   110→
   111→### STORY-001: Convert Display Text to URL Slug
   112→**As a** developer
   113→**I want** to convert user-provided display text into a URL-safe slug
   114→**So that** I can generate clean, readable URLs from arbitrary input
   115→
   116→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   117→- GIVEN user input "Hello, World!"
   118→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   119→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   120→
   121→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers with Underscores
   122→**As a** developer

   125→
   126→**Acceptance Criteria**:

   128→- WHEN I call `slugify("  Foo__Bar  ")`
   129→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   130→
   131→### STORY-003: Clean Up Messy Input with Repeated Separators
   132→**As a** developer
   133→**I want** to collapse repeated hyphens from filtered characters
   134→**So that** the output is clean and readable
   135→
   136→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   137→- GIVEN user input "a---b" (multiple hyphens)
   138→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   139→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   140→
   141→## Test Cases
   142→
   143→| Input | Expected Output | Validates |
   144→|-------|----------------|-----------|
   145→| `"Hello, World!"` | `"hello-world"` | REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-005 |
   146→| `"  Foo__Bar  "` | `"foo-bar"` | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-005 |
   147→| `"a---b"` | `"a-b"` | REQ-004 |
   148→| `"Test123"` | `"test123"` | REQ-001, REQ-003 |
   149→| `"---trim---"` | `"trim"` | REQ-005 |
   150→| `"multiple   spaces"` | `"multiple-spaces"` | REQ-002, REQ-004 |
   151→| `"Special!@#$%Chars"` | `"specialchars"` | REQ-003 |
   152→| `""` (empty string) | `""` | Edge case handling |
   153→
   154→## Constraints
   155→
   156→**Technical Constraints**:
   157→- Must be implementable as a pure function (no side effects)
   158→- Must handle empty string input gracefully
   159→- Must be compatible with TypeScript strict mode
   160→
   161→**Business Constraints**:
   162→- Must process input in a single pass for performance
   163→- Must produce deterministic output (same input always produces same output)
   164→
   165→## Success Criteria
   166→
   167→The feature is complete when:
   168→1. The `slugify` function is implemented and exported
   169→2. All test cases in the table above pass
   170→3. The function handles edge cases (empty strings, all-special-characters)
   171→4. Unit tests verify all requirements
   172→5. The function integrates into the existing `src/utils.ts` module
   173→
   174→## Out of Scope
   175→
   176→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   177→- Unicode character normalization (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents)
   178→- Configurable separator characters (hyphen is fixed)
   179→- Maximum length enforcement

/**
 * Add two numbers.
 */
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}

/**
 * Convert arbitrary text into a URL-safe, hyphenated slug.
 *
 * Applies the following transformations in sequence:
 * 1. Convert to lowercase
 * 2. Replace spaces and underscores with hyphens
 * 3. Remove characters that are not letters, digits, or hyphens
 * 4. Collapse consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
 * 5. Trim leading and trailing hyphens
 *
 * @param text - The input text to slugify
 * @returns A URL-safe slug string
 */
export function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')
    .replace(/-+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-|-$/g, '');
}

     4→# Feature Requirements: slugify-utility
     5→
     6→---
     7→rp1_run_id: 2ca070d6-4557-42a2-b4a2-badacf24440d
     8→---
     9→
    10→## Overview
    11→
    12→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    13→**Status**: Requirements Defined
    14→**Priority**: Must Have
    15→
    16→This feature provides a text normalization utility that converts arbitrary text input into URL-safe, hyphenated slug format suitable for identifiers, filenames, and routing.
    17→
    18→## Business Context
    19→
    20→String slugification is a common requirement across web applications for:
    21→- Generating URL-friendly identifiers from user input
    22→- Creating consistent file naming from arbitrary text
    23→- Normalizing text for searching and indexing
    24→
    25→## Requirements
    26→
    27→### REQ-001: Text Case Normalization
    28→**Priority**: Must Have
    29→**User Type**: Developer
    30→**Description**: The utility must convert all alphabetic characters in the input text to lowercase.
    31→
    32→**Rationale**: Consistent lowercase formatting ensures URL and identifier uniqueness regardless of input casing (e.g., "Hello" and "HELLO" produce the same slug).
    33→
    34→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    35→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    36→- Lowercase letters remain unchanged
    37→- Non-alphabetic characters are unaffected by case normalization
    38→- Mixed-case input like "Hello, World!" produces lowercase output
    39→
    40→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    41→**Priority**: Must Have
    42→**User Type**: Developer
    43→**Description**: The utility must replace all space characters and underscore characters with single hyphens.
    44→
    45→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard separator in URL slugs and kebab-case identifiers. Spaces are invalid in URLs, and underscores need normalization to a single separator type.
    46→
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Single space characters are replaced with single hyphens
    49→- Multiple consecutive spaces are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    50→- Underscore characters are replaced with single hyphens
    51→- Multiple consecutive underscores are replaced with single hyphens (collapsed)
    52→- Mixed spaces and underscores are normalized to single hyphens
    53→
    54→### REQ-003: Character Filtering
    55→**Priority**: Must Have
    56→**User Type**: Developer
    57→**Description**: The utility must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), digit (0-9), or hyphen (-).
    58→
    59→**Rationale**: URL-safe slugs should contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens. Special characters, punctuation, and symbols must be stripped to ensure compatibility across systems.
    60→
    61→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    62→- Alphabetic characters (a-z after lowercasing) are retained
    63→- Numeric digits (0-9) are retained
    64→- Hyphens (-) are retained
    65→- All punctuation (!, ?, ., ,, etc.) is removed
    66→- All special characters (@, #, $, %, etc.) is removed
    67→- Unicode characters outside basic Latin are removed
    68→
    69→### REQ-004: Hyphen Collapse
    70→**Priority**: Must Have
    71→**User Type**: Developer
    72→**Description**: The utility must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    73→
    74→**Rationale**: Consecutive hyphens may result from multiple filtering and replacement operations. Collapsing ensures clean, readable output without repeated separators.
    75→
    76→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    77→- Two consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
    78→- Three or more consecutive hyphens are reduced to one hyphen
    79→- Single hyphens remain unchanged
    80→- Hyphen collapsing occurs after all character filtering and replacement
    81→
    82→### REQ-005: Edge Trimming
    83→**Priority**: Must Have
    84→**User Type**: Developer
    85→**Description**: The utility must remove any leading or trailing hyphens from the output.
    86→
    87→**Rationale**: Slugs should not begin or end with separators. Trimming ensures clean output suitable for use in URLs, file paths, and identifiers.
    88→
    89→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    90→- Leading hyphens are removed from the beginning of the output
    91→- Trailing hyphens are removed from the end of the output
    92→- Multiple leading or trailing hyphens are all removed
    93→- Internal hyphens are preserved
    94→- Trimming occurs as the final transformation step
    95→
    96→### REQ-006: Function Signature
    97→**Priority**: Must Have
    98→**User Type**: Developer
    99→**Description**: The utility must be exposed as a function named `slugify` that accepts a single text parameter and returns the slugified string.
   100→
   101→**Rationale**: A clear, simple function signature ensures ease of use and integration into existing TypeScript/JavaScript codebases.
   102→
   103→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   104→- Function is named `slugify`
   105→- Function accepts one parameter representing the input text
   106→- Function returns a string representing the slugified output
   107→- Function is exported for use by other modules
   108→
   109→## User Stories
   110→
   111→### STORY-001: Convert Display Text to URL Slug
   112→**As a** developer
   113→**I want** to convert user-provided display text into a URL-safe slug
   114→**So that** I can generate clean, readable URLs from arbitrary input
   115→
   116→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   117→- GIVEN user input "Hello, World!"
   118→- WHEN I call `slugify("Hello, World!")`
   119→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   120→
   121→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers with Underscores
   122→**As a** developer
   123→**I want** to normalize identifiers that use underscores
   124→**So that** I can convert snake_case or mixed formats to kebab-case
   125→
   126→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   127→- GIVEN user input "Foo__Bar" (with multiple underscores and spaces)
   128→- WHEN I call `slugify("  Foo__Bar  ")`
   129→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   130→
   131→### STORY-003: Clean Up Messy Input with Repeated Separators
   132→**As a** developer
   133→**I want** to collapse repeated hyphens from filtered characters
   134→**So that** the output is clean and readable
   135→
   136→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   137→- GIVEN user input "a---b" (multiple hyphens)
   138→- WHEN I call `slugify("a---b")`
   139→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   140→
   141→## Test Cases
   142→
   143→| Input | Expected Output | Validates |
   144→|-------|----------------|-----------|
   145→| `"Hello, World!"` | `"hello-world"` | REQ-001, REQ-003, REQ-005 |
   146→| `"  Foo__Bar  "` | `"foo-bar"` | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-005 |
   147→| `"a---b"` | `"a-b"` | REQ-004 |
   148→| `"Test123"` | `"test123"` | REQ-001, REQ-003 |
   149→| `"---trim---"` | `"trim"` | REQ-005 |
   150→| `"multiple   spaces"` | `"multiple-spaces"` | REQ-002, REQ-004 |
   151→| `"Special!@#$%Chars"` | `"specialchars"` | REQ-003 |
   152→| `""` (empty string) | `""` | Edge case handling |
   153→
   154→## Constraints
   155→
   156→**Technical Constraints**:
   157→- Must be implementable as a pure function (no side effects)
   158→- Must handle empty string input gracefully
   159→- Must be compatible with TypeScript strict mode
   160→
   161→**Business Constraints**:
   162→- Must process input in a single pass for performance
   163→- Must produce deterministic output (same input always produces same output)
   164→
   165→## Success Criteria
   166→
   167→The feature is complete when:
   168→1. The `slugify` function is implemented and exported
   169→2. All test cases in the table above pass
   170→3. The function handles edge cases (empty strings, all-special-characters)
   171→4. Unit tests verify all requirements
   172→5. The function integrates into the existing `src/utils.ts` module
   173→

   175→
   176→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   177→- Unicode character normalization (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents)
   178→- Configurable separator characters (hyphen is fixed)
   179→- Maximum length enforcement
